title: How 'Spider-Noir' VFX Team Made the Show Look Amazing—With No Room for Mistakes
summary: Imagine you're building a giant LEGO set, but you can't change anything once you start. That's what it was like for the visual effects (VFX) team on 'Spider-Noir,' a new show on Prime Video starring Nicolas Cage. The VFX supervisor, Hnedel Maximore, explained that many scenes mixed real stunts with computer effects. That meant every move had to be planned perfectly. 'We had a lot of technical, timing things that are highly dependent on stunts and special effects,' he said. 'You have to be dogmatic about it because otherwise you blow your budget, or you lose the tone of the show.' Dogmatic (dog-MAT-ic) means sticking to a plan no matter what. The show is set in 1930s New York, where Ben Reilly (Nicolas Cage) is a private investigator who also fights crime as Spider-Man. With eight episodes, the team had to previsualize (pre-VIZ-oo-uh-lize) key scenes—like drawing a storyboard before filming—and then stick to it. No improvising! So next time you watch an action scene, remember: it took a lot of careful planning to make it look so cool.
why_it_matters: Planning ahead carefully, like for a school play or science fair, can help you avoid mistakes and make your project amazing.
